# fshy: Domains and DNS in full

> Managed DNS, free domains and certificate authorities.

Data as of 2026-11-10, the date of the published data. Version `e7cf1b4a40af`: the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of every record's Markdown, topic by topic in the one order (hosted before self-hosted, then verdict, provider name, record id); it changes whenever a record does.

How to read a record, and the other topics: https://fshy.ajam.dev/llms-full.txt. One line per record: https://fshy.ajam.dev/t/domains-dns.md.

## Cloudflare DNS

- `domains-dns/cloudflare-dns` | qualifies | evidence measured | binding per-object-cap | category managed authoritative DNS
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-22T03:05:00.000Z (live) | stale on 2027-01-21
- url https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudflare.md
- free tier: free zone on any plan with anycast resolution, an API, DNSSEC and 200 records per zone on zones created on or after 2024-09-01 | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1] | note: 1,000 records per zone on zones created before 2024-09-01
- per-object cap: 200 DNS records per zone on a zone created on or after 2024-09-01; 1,000 on an older free zone; 3,500 on Pro and Business | source: [1] | note: records that other Cloudflare services add, such as Email Routing TXT and MX, count toward the same quota
- retention: the zone persists while it is active; a zone whose nameservers stop pointing at Cloudflare moves to a Moved state and is deleted after a long enough period | source: [2]
- egress: DNS queries are never limited or capped on any plan | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: a Cloudflare account, and the domain must use Cloudflare nameservers
- interface: rest, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 200 records per zone on a free zone created on or after 2024-09-01 [1]
  - request-rate: the API is rate limited per account; the published DNS limit is on queries, and there are none [2]
- limits note: the dashboard warns at 85% of the record quota and the current quota and usage are readable per zone through the API
- interface detail: a REST API for zones and records; a DoH and DoT resolver at cloudflare-dns.com; flarectl and the Cloudflare Terraform provider
- tooling: the Cloudflare API, flarectl, Terraform, certbot with a DNS-01 plugin, acme.sh
- composes with: the only free DNS in this set that also gives a free CDN, a free tunnel, free Universal SSL and free Email Routing on the same zone
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: 200 records is the number a per-tenant subdomain scheme meets, and it is shared with the records Cloudflare adds for Email Routing. The absence of a query cap is what makes it the default choice.
- evidence note: the keyless DoH resolver answered a real query, and the record quota and the apex CNAME behaviour are both first-party pages. No zone was created.
- evidence:
  - probe:https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=example.com&type=A 2026-10-22: 200, 251 bytes of JSON with Status 0 and two A records, so the keyless DoH endpoint answers programmatically without an account
  - [1] 2026-10-22: Per-zone quota: Free zones created before 2024-09-01 00:00:00 UTC 1,000; Free zones created on or after 2024-09-01 200; Pro 3,500; Business 3,500; Enterprise per-account. Records created by other Cloudflare services count toward the quota
  - [3] 2026-10-22: 'Cloudflare's CNAME flattening allows you to create CNAME records at your zone apex'; an ANAME or ALIAS at a previous provider can be recreated as a CNAME at @
  - [2] 2026-10-22: 'Cloudflare never limits or caps DNS queries'; a zone in a Moved state for long enough is deleted
- sources:
  - [1] https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/
  - [2] https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/faq/
  - [3] https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/how-to/create-zone-apex/

## deSEC

- `domains-dns/desec` | qualifies | evidence reported | binding write-gated | category managed authoritative DNS with a full REST API
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T00:20:29.067Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-19
- url https://desec.io/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/desec.md
- free tier: free managed DNS with anycast, a full REST API, DNSSEC and no published query cap; the number of domains an account may hold is a per-account limit_domains value that deSEC does not publish as a fixed number: unless set explicitly it grows with the domains delegated to deSEC with DNSSEC enabled | unit: objects | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no published record count cap; the binding limits are the domain count per account and the RRset change rate per domain
- retention: zones persist while the account is active; a domain not renewed is deleted after a grace period | source: [1]
- egress: no query cap is published; the metered quantity is API requests | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: email signup; a token per account
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate: RRset create, delete or modify: 2 per second, 15 per minute, 100 per hour, 300 per day, per domain [2]
  - request-rate: any authenticated or unauthenticated activity: 2,000 per day per account or per IP [2]
  - request-rate: dynDNS updates: 2 per 2 minutes per domain [2]
  - write-gated (binding): no fixed number is published: the per-account maximum is the read-only limit_domains field of the account object (the API reference example shows 15) and, unless deSEC has set a limit for the account explicitly, it grows with the domains delegated to deSEC with DNSSEC enabled; Names under dedyn.io are limited to 1 per account. A new account is reported to start at one, and a deSEC staff reply gives the formula max(1, s + round(sqrt(s))) for s DNSSEC-delegated domains [3]
- limits note: DNS reads are 10/s and 50/min; domain creation and deletion are 10/s, 300/min and 1,000/h; account actions with external effects are 3/min; a 429 carries Retry-After and the windows slide
- binding note: the change rate is generous for steady state. The domain counter is what stops a multi-zone scheme: it is not published, a new account is reported to begin at one domain, and raising it is a support request with a person in the queue.
- interface detail: a REST API with token authentication; the API speaks RRsets rather than individual records, and an empty subname is the zone apex
- tooling: the deSEC API directly, DNSControl, certbot and acme.sh with a DNS-01 hook, Terraform
- composes with: one small zone with a real API, and a support request per additional domain; the domain counter is what constrains a multi-zone scheme, not the change rate
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The 300 changes a day per domain is generous for steady state and painful for provisioning: a 500-record import takes two days. Bulk endpoints exist and the docs recommend them, which is the alternative route. The domain counter is the constraint that is often recorded as 'no published cap', which is a different claim: deSEC publishes no fixed number, and its own forum gives one. The cap binds before the rate table does, and only a signup shows the number an account actually receives.
- evidence note: the API, the rate table and the account reference are first-party. The account reference documents the per-account domain limit (limit_domains) and how it grows with DNSSEC-delegated domains, and the domains reference documents the 403 on reaching it, but neither states a fixed number; the initial value of one and the staff formula come from deSEC's forum and an independent write-up, at the reported rung. free_tier.unit is objects, not unlimited, because the domain count is capped.
- evidence:
  - probe:https://desec.io/api/v1/domains/ 2026-10-22: 401, 58 bytes, 'Authentication credentials were not provided.', with WWW-Authenticate: Token and Allow: GET, POST, HEAD, OPTIONS. The endpoint exists and is token-authenticated
  - probe:https://desec.io/api/v1/auth/login/ 2026-10-22: 400 with '{"email":["This field is required."],"password":["This field is required."]}', a live DRF login endpoint
  - [2] 2026-10-22: dns_api_per_domain_expensive 2/s 15/min 100/h 300/day for RRset creation, deletion and modification per domain; user 2,000/day; dyndns 2/2min per domain; throttled requests return 429 with Retry-After
  - [4] 2026-10-22: 'If subname is empty, this is equal to {name}.' so the apex is addressable; a wildcard component is allowed once at the beginning of the name
  - [5] 2026-10-22: a deSEC staff reply: 'the limit is max(1, s + round(sqrt(s))), were s is the number of domains delegated to us with DNSSEC enabled', giving 6 for s=4
  - [6] 2026-10-22: 'New accounts are limited to one domain and there is a note when you add a domain: Contact support to apply for a higher limit.'
  - [7] 2026-10-22: an independent account: 'there is an initial limit of 1 domain per account. Right below is the note Contact support to apply for a higher limit.'
  - [8] 2026-10-22: the signup form says only 'Your first domain (you can add more later)', which is the closest thing to a published statement and gives no number
  - [3] 2026-11-03: the per-account domain limit (limit_domains) is not a fixed published number: it grows with the DNSSEC-delegated domains unless deSEC sets it explicitly | capture: sha256:ff57a1a792e0a7cf6ae782ca2b96401625088d13e90ab1bcf30b76f28827f425 | quote: Unless we have set a limit for your account explicitly, this number grows with the domains you have delegated to us securely (with DNSSEC enabled).
  - [3] 2026-11-03: limit_domains is a read-only per-account field in the account object, the maximum number of domains the user can create | capture: sha256:ff57a1a792e0a7cf6ae782ca2b96401625088d13e90ab1bcf30b76f28827f425 | quote: Maximum number of domains the user can create.
  - [9] 2026-11-03: the API enforces a per-account maximum and answers 403 when it is reached | capture: sha256:6506f0790ed2b9a146b4c09ccaf796724a72402c43e0cc9b9b6887cf22612257 | quote: If you have reached the maximum number of domains for your account, the API responds with `403 Forbidden`.
  - [9] 2026-11-03: names under dedyn.io are limited to 1 per account | capture: sha256:6506f0790ed2b9a146b4c09ccaf796724a72402c43e0cc9b9b6887cf22612257 | quote: Domains that we offer for registration ourselves, such as those directly under `dedyn.io`, are limited to one per account.
- sources:
  - [1] https://desec.io/
  - [2] https://desec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rate-limits.html
  - [3] https://desec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/auth/account.html
  - [4] https://desec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dns/rrsets.html
  - [5] https://talk.desec.io/t/feedback-about-recent-limit-changes/1834
  - [6] https://talk.desec.io/t/how-to-apply-for-a-spot/1370
  - [7] https://yepoleb.at/blog/2025/10/27/my-experience-with-desec/
  - [8] https://desec.io/signup
  - [9] https://desec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/dns/domains.html

## Let's Encrypt

- `domains-dns/lets-encrypt` | qualifies | evidence measured | binding request-rate | category certificate authority
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-22T03:05:00.000Z (live) | stale on 2027-01-21
- url https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/letsencrypt.md
- free tier: free 90-day certificates including wildcards over DNS-01, with automated issuance and renewal | unit: unlimited | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no certificate size cap; the binding limits are rate limits and not object caps
- retention: a certificate is valid 90 days and must be renewed; ARI lets a client renew early | days: 90 | source: [1]
- egress: no charge | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: anonymous | detail: no account is required to obtain a certificate; an ACME account key is generated locally and is not a registration
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 50 certificates per registered domain per 7 days, global across all accounts, refilling at 1 per 202 minutes [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 5 certificates per exact set of identifiers per 7 days [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 300 new orders per account per 3 hours [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 10 new accounts per IP per 3 hours [2]
  - request-rate (binding): 5 failed authorizations per identifier per account per hour; 1,152 consecutive failures then the identifier pauses [2]
  - retention-clamped: a certificate is valid 90 days; the requesting client performs the renewal and no automatic extension exists [1]
- interface detail: the ACME v2 protocol at acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org, with a staging endpoint for testing
- tooling: certbot, acme.sh, lego, Caddy, Traefik, any ACME client
- composes with: free TLS on any name you control, including a wildcard, which is what makes the free-DNS plus free-tunnel chain terminate in a valid certificate
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The per-registered-domain limit is the one that binds a multi-tenant scheme: 50 certificates a week for every name under one registered domain, whoever requests them. The exact-identifier limit is the one that binds a retry loop, and 5 an hour is reachable in a bad afternoon.
- evidence note: the production and staging directories were fetched and answered 200 with the profile list; the rate limits are a first-party page. The 90-day validity is on the FAQ page, not on the rate-limits page it was attributed to.
- evidence:
  - probe:https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory 2026-10-22: 200, 961 bytes, sha256 ee1bfe324dcd5aff6e67ba25ea98397494d5b6ebf6c7f16e98348254636190e0, listing keyChange, the classic, shortlived and tlsserver profiles, and the current subscriber agreement URL
  - probe:https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory 2026-10-22: 200, 1,035 bytes; the staging endpoint is live, so an issuance test costs nothing against the production limits
  - [2] 2026-10-22: 50 certificates per registered domain per 7 days; 5 per exact set of identifiers per 7 days; 300 new orders per account per 3 hours; 10 accounts per IP per 3 hours; 5 failed authorizations per identifier per hour; 1,152 consecutive failures; ARI renewals are exempt from the order and per-domain limits
  - [1] 2026-10-22: 'Our default certificates are valid for 90 days'; the same FAQ points at the published rationale
- sources:
  - [1] https://letsencrypt.org/docs/faq/
  - [2] https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/

## Namecheap FreeDNS

- `domains-dns/namecheap-freedns` | qualifies | evidence reported | binding write-gated | category managed authoritative DNS
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-22T03:05:00.000Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-06
- url https://www.namecheap.com/domains/freedns/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/namecheap.md
- free tier: free DNS hosting for domains registered elsewhere, with dynamic DNS | unit: unlimited | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no record count is published on Namecheap's own page; comparison sites state about 150 host records, which is a third-party figure | source: [1] | note: the record is reported on this field, and the 150 comes from comparison sites rather than from the page named here; the page named here is the one that is silent
- retention: the zone persists while it is configured; verification of nameserver changes takes up to 16 hours and the registrar gives 10 days to make the change | source: [1]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: email signup; the domain must be registered elsewhere
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: no published record count; comparison sites state about 150 host records, which is reported and not documented [1]
  - write-gated (binding): third-party domains only, and nameserver verification takes up to 16 hours [1]
- interface detail: a web panel; an API exists for registered domains and is not documented for FreeDNS
- tooling: the web panel; dynamic DNS by URL
- composes with: a backup DNS for a domain whose primary is elsewhere, which is the use Namecheap itself names
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The 150-record figure cannot be promoted to documented until a zone is created and counted, and creating one needs a domain registered elsewhere.
- evidence note: Namecheap's page proves the service and the third-party-domain rule but not the record count, which is a comparison-page figure. A record count from a comparison page is not a quota.
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: 'Free 3rd-party domains support only'; nameserver verification within 16 hours; 10 days to change nameservers at the current registrar. No record count is stated
- sources:
  - [1] https://www.namecheap.com/domains/freedns/

## afraid.org FreeDNS

- `domains-dns/afraid-freedns` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category shared-registry subdomains and managed DNS
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-02T10:17:37.729Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-03
- url https://freedns.afraid.org/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/afraid.md
- free tier: unlimited domains per account with 20 free subdomains on each, plus 5 free hostnames on a shared registry of 23,087 domains | unit: unlimited | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-11-02 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 5 hostnames on the shared registry and 20 subdomains on each domain you own, on the free plan | note: the paid plans raise the subdomain cap to 50, 100, 250 or 500 and add wildcard records, which the free plan lacks
- retention: a hosted domain that stays undelegated (broken) for 365 days is disabled; a shared-registry hostname lasts only while its domain stays in the registry, which the FAQ says may disappear next week | source: [2]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [3]
- identity: email | detail: a first and last name, a user ID, a password and an e-mail address that receives the activation link, an image captcha, and a required checkbox declaring the user is not on a U.S. restricted list or in a U.S.-sanctioned territory; no phone and no card (https://freedns.afraid.org/signup/)
- interface: unknown
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: 5 free shared-registry hostnames and 20 subdomains on each domain you own [1]
  - write-gated (binding): a hostname on a Shared: Private domain can be rejected by that domain's owner, while a Shared: Public domain takes hostnames without the owner's approval [2]
  - write-gated (binding): the free plan keeps captchas, which every paid plan removes; the pricing table does not say which actions they guard [4]
- interface detail: no general record-management API is documented, and the /api/ page is behind a login, so its content is unverified: behind a sign-up; the site's client list says a client that sends a SHA1 hash of the user name and password can fetch the needed update URL itself; the free plan's programmatic path is the dynamic-update URL https://sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/ (https://v6.sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/ for IPv6), which changes the address of an existing record; other record edits, TXT included, are POSTs to https://freedns.afraid.org/subdomain/save.php with a logged-in session cookie; the interface term for the update URL would be dyndns, which the vocabulary lacks, so interface carries unknown
- tooling: curl against sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/; DD-WRT and router integrations
- composes with: a free hostname that resolves without owning a domain, which is the only thing here that does
- reliability: a shared-registry name is on someone else's domain, so its survival is their decision
- notes: The name is not yours and the owner can withdraw consent. It is a dynamic-DNS tool with a social dependency, not a name.
- evidence note: the landing, features, pricing, signup, signup Q&A and FAQ pages were read and quoted; the shared-registry cap of 5 hostnames and the 20-subdomain cap on an owned domain are first-party figures
- evidence:
  - [3] 2026-10-22: '23,246 domains in the shared domain registry'; dynamic update by URL token at sync.afraid.org/u/<token>/; free and premium subdomain and domain hosting
  - [5] 2026-10-22: the registry is a browsable list of domains a hostname may be attached to
  - [1] 2026-10-30: an account may host any number of owned domains; the same page counts 23,097 shared-registry domains | capture: sha256:8227876238a766b38022311fce710cb30bc8a342741b8dd7a98550017148f564 | quote: Unlimited number of domains per account (yes really)
  - [1] 2026-10-30: a free account gets 5 hostnames on the shared registry, a first-party figure | capture: sha256:8227876238a766b38022311fce710cb30bc8a342741b8dd7a98550017148f564 | quote: Comes with 5 free hostnames that work in the shared domain registry
  - [4] 2026-10-30: the subdomain cap is 5 on the free plan and 50, 100, 250 or 500 on the four paid plans | capture: sha256:4e93846147e892623809ea394a6d8335282bd20a0601d7e4a7717b6b6f31c5f6 | quote: Subdomain cap 5 50 100 250 500
  - [1] 2026-10-30: each domain the user owns gets 20 free subdomains | capture: sha256:8227876238a766b38022311fce710cb30bc8a342741b8dd7a98550017148f564 | quote: 20 free subdomains included on each of your own domains

## Cloudflare Universal SSL

- `domains-dns/cloudflare-universal-ssl` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence reported | binding per-object-cap | category certificate authority
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-09T05:04:38.024Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-24
- url https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudflare.md
- free tier: a free certificate on every zone, covering the apex and one level of subdomain | unit: unlimited | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: covers example.com and app.example.com, not a.b.example.com; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager | source: [1]
- retention: the certificate is issued and renewed by Cloudflare while the zone is active | source: [1]
- egress: no charge | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: a Cloudflare account and a zone on Cloudflare nameservers
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): one level of subdomain only; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager [1]
- interface detail: automatic on a proxied zone; no client API of its own, and the zone API reports the certificate
- tooling: nothing to run: the certificate appears on the zone
- composes with: the certificate half of the free endpoint, from the same account and zone as the DNS and the tunnel
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The one-level limit is the trap. A per-tenant scheme at tenant.app.example.com needs a paid certificate manager, or a wildcard from Let's Encrypt over DNS-01, which is free.
- evidence note: the one-level coverage limit is stated across Cloudflare's TLS documentation and repeated in third-party summaries; the product page was reached only as a stub, so this is reported.
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-10-22: Universal SSL is free on every plan; the one-level subdomain coverage limit and the Advanced Certificate Manager upgrade path are the substance
  - [1] 2026-11-09: on a full setup the certificate covers the apex and first-level subdomains only | capture: sha256:c6274db1c947c6f3ba83385ab5db05c1de2cc8322821c8be77cf7ba022688cdd | quote: On a full setup, Universal SSL certificates cover your root domain (for example, `example.com`) and first-level subdomains (for example, `www.example.com`).
- sources:
  - [1] https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/universal-ssl/

## ClouDNS

- `domains-dns/cloudns-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category managed authoritative DNS
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-02T10:17:37.731Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-03
- url https://www.cloudns.net/managed-dns/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/cloudns.md
- free tier: Free Forever: 1 DNS zone, 50 DNS records, 500,000 queries per month, 1 mail forward, 1 dynamic DNS hostname, 4 unicast nameservers | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 50 DNS records and 1 zone | source: [1] | note: the tightest record cap in this class
- retention: a zone with no DNS queries for over 30 days can be deleted without notice, the free plan named in particular | days: 30 | source: [2]
- egress: 500,000 DNS queries per month on Free, the only published query cap in this class | metered: yes | free allowance: 500,000 queries per month | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: a first and last name, an e-mail address, a password and an hCaptcha; no phone and no card on the signup form (https://www.cloudns.net/index/show/signup/); an identity verification can be requested after signup
- interface: unknown
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 1 zone and 50 records [1]
  - request-rate: 500,000 DNS queries per month [1]
  - retention-clamped: a zone with no DNS queries for over 30 days can be deleted without notice [2]
- interface detail: the HTTP API at https://api.cloudns.net/ (auth-id and auth-password) manages zones and records, but the plan table marks HTTP API access absent on Free and present from Premium S at $2.95/month; the free plan's programmatic path is the DynURL of its one dynamic hostname, https://ipv4.cloudns.net/api/dynamicURL/?q=<token> (the ipv6.cloudns.net host for an AAAA record), which belongs to one A or AAAA record whose Dynamic URL is activated in the panel and changes the address of that record; its interface term would be dyndns, which the vocabulary lacks, so interface carries unknown
- tooling: on Free, curl or wget against the DynURL from cron, and the wiki's DynURL guides for Windows, Linux, Synology, MikroTik and pfSense; the HTTP API needs a paid plan
- composes with: the plan table gives Free no secondary DNS zones and no zone transfers, which rules out an AXFR pairing with another provider but not a second provider whose records are mirrored by hand
- reliability: a zone with no DNS queries for over 30 days, or a Free zone delegated to non-ClouDNS nameservers, can be suspended or deleted without notice
- notes: The Free plan holds 1 DNS zone and 50 DNS records.
- evidence note: the managed-DNS page was read and states the Free Forever column explicitly.

## DigitalPlat FreeDomain

- `domains-dns/digitalplat-freedomain` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category free registrable subdomain
- identity a placeholder: card and phone unknown | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:10.325Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://github.com/DigitalPlatDev/FreeDomain | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/github-digitalplatdev.md
- free tier: free registration under the suffixes .DPDNS.ORG, .US.KG, .QZZ.IO, .XX.KG and .QD.JE, with the user's own authoritative nameservers entered in the dashboard; the default limit is 1 domain per user account | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 1 domain per user account by default; sub-subdomains under the assigned name are made at the user's DNS provider
- retention: the dashboard is the source of truth for status and expiration date; renewal windows, fees and slot rules are not stated on the pages read and are said to change | source: [2]
- egress: no query cap published; the service holds no zone, so queries go to the user's chosen DNS provider | metered: no | source: [3]
- identity: any-phone | detail: the account tutorial's preparation list names an email address, a name, a valid phone number in the format the form requests and a complete contact address; the dashboard registration form itself was not read: unverified whether the phone is checked by a code
- interface: unknown
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): the default limit is 1 domain per user account [4]
  - write-gated: supported suffixes, registration pauses, slot requirements, prices and limits change, and a registration may consume a slot or create a charge; a third-party report says .US.KG and .XX.KG paused new registrations and .QZZ.IO went paid-only, while the repository still lists them [5]
- binding note: 1 domain per account is the stated cap, and the operator reserves registration pauses and slot or charge requirements per suffix; the zone is the registrant's through delegation, and the suffix listing keeps the TLS limit per name
- interface detail: a web dashboard at dash.domain.digitalplat.org that needs an account (unverified: behind a sign-up); the tutorial has an API chapter whose content was not read. The service stores only the delegation: A, CNAME, MX and TXT records are managed at the external DNS service the nameservers name
- tooling: the DigitalPlat dashboard, then an external authoritative DNS service of the user's choice
- composes with: the delegation can point at an external DNS service such as Cloudflare, which makes the name a zone of the registrant's; the suffix is on the Public Suffix List
- reliability: the operator can pause a suffix, change slots or charges, or suspend a domain, and a third party reports two suffixes paused and one gone paid-only
- notes: The zone is the registrant's: the service stores only NS delegation, so a Cloudflare zone or any DNS host can serve it. The operator can still withdraw it, because a suffix can be paused, put behind a slot or charge, or a domain suspended. The TLS limit does not bind, because the suffixes are listed and each name counts alone. The dashboard is behind a login wall, so the live slot and renewal rules are unverified.
- evidence note: the repository README, FAQ and tutorial pages were read and quoted; the dashboard answered a login wall, so the live registration form, the current slot rule and the renewal terms are unverified; the suffix status report is third-party

- `domains-dns/dnspod-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category managed authoritative DNS | tier Free
- needs card no, phone yes, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:07.606Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://docs.dnspod.com/dns/help-diff-plan/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/dnspod.md
- free tier: the Free DNS plan: unlimited records, 5 subdomain levels, 2 URL forwards, round-robin DNS of up to 10 records per host, API supported, minimum TTL 600 s; it is activated by default once a domain is added | unit: unlimited | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no record cap on the Free plan (records unlimited); 5 subdomain levels, 2 URL forwards and up to 10 round-robin records per host | source: [1]
- retention: unverified: the plan, overview and API pages read state no inactivity, renewal or confirmation rule for a Free zone | source: [1]

  - per-object-cap (binding): 5 subdomain levels, 2 URL forwards, up to 10 round-robin records per host, minimum TTL 600 s on the Free plan [1]
- binding note: the 600 s TTL floor decides for a dynamic record; the identity gate is a phone number with an SMS code

- tooling: curl or any HTTP client against the DNSPod API, and the DNSPod console; an update must name the domain_id and the record_id
- composes with: a free zone for a domain the user already owns, with A, CNAME and subdomain records pointed at any address; it can hold a dynamic record but the 600 s minimum TTL slows how quickly an address change reaches resolvers
- reliability: unverified: the pages read state no inactivity rule and no SLA for the Free plan
- notes: Confirmation interval: none stated. The mainland-China site dnspod.cn has its own e-mail registration that also binds and verifies a mobile number.

## DuckDNS

- `domains-dns/duckdns` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence measured | binding per-object-cap | category free dynamic subdomain
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-02T10:17:37.731Z (live) | stale on 2027-02-01
- url https://www.duckdns.org/spec.jsp | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/duckdns.md
- free tier: subdomains under duckdns.org with a token API, IPv4, IPv6 and TXT support | unit: unlimited | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: the number of subdomains per account is about 5, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number
- retention: a record persists until updated or cleared with clear=true, provided the account is used | source: [1]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: Google, GitHub or Reddit OAuth
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): about 5 subdomains, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number [1]
- interface detail: a single HTTPS GET per update; the token is a query parameter
- tooling: curl, any DDNS client, a router's built-in DuckDNS provider
- composes with: a name for a home IP or a tunnel endpoint, and nothing else: no certificate automation and no proxying
- reliability: a bad token returns HTTP 200 with the body KO, so a status-only check reports success on a failed update
- notes: A DuckDNS name cannot be a Cloudflare zone, so it cannot carry a Tunnel, Email Routing or Universal SSL. It is a dynamic-DNS tool, not a name a service can live on.
- evidence note: the update endpoint was called today with an empty token and answered 200 KO, which proves both the endpoint and the failure shape. The subdomain cap is third-party.
- evidence:
  - probe:https://www.duckdns.org/update?domains=example&token=&ip= 2026-10-22: 200 with a two-byte body 'KO'. A 200 is not success; the rejection is in the body
  - [1] 2026-10-22: the update URL, IPv4 and IPv6 parameters, the TXT form, and clear=true to delete records; a TXT record applies to all sub-subdomains under the name
  - [1] 2026-11-02: the update is a single HTTPS GET to DuckDNS | capture: sha256:e44c623b17f38e48ed7e76eb9c55006a3474059f47c69f325427ad54cdedb50f | quote: You can update your domain(s) with a single HTTPS get to DuckDNS
  - [1] 2026-11-02: clear=true makes the update call clear the IPv4 and IPv6 values of the named subnames instead of setting them | capture: sha256:e44c623b17f38e48ed7e76eb9c55006a3474059f47c69f325427ad54cdedb50f | quote: clear - OPTIONAL - if set to true, the update will ignore all ip's and clear both your records
  - [1] 2026-11-02: the update call is a GET to duckdns.org/update with the subnames and the account token as query parameters | capture: sha256:e44c623b17f38e48ed7e76eb9c55006a3474059f47c69f325427ad54cdedb50f | quote: https://www.duckdns.org/update?domains={YOURVALUE}&token={YOURVALUE}[&ip={YOURVALUE}][&ipv6={YOURVALUE}][&verbose=true][&clear=true]

## Dynu

- `domains-dns/dynu-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category free dynamic DNS and managed DNS | tier Free

- per-object cap: 4 hostnames and up to 4 subdomains on the free plan per the FAQ; the membership page says members can have more than 3 third level domain names and 200 custom records, and no page read gives a free custom-record count (unverified) | source: [1]
- retention: Dynu accounts never expire; a free dynamic DNS service stays fully functional until the user deletes it | source: [2]
- egress: no DNS query cap published on the pages read | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: the sign-up form asks for a first name, a last name, a username, a password and an e-mail address entered twice, or a sign-up with GitHub or Google; no phone or card field in the captured form text (https://www.dynu.com/en-US/ControlPanel/CreateAccount)
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): 4 hostnames and 4 subdomains free; the membership page's own figure is more than 3 third level domain names for members [1]
  - per-object-cap (binding): up to 20 hostnames in one update request (numhost above 20) [3]
  - write-gated: several record types are member-only, among them CAA on a third-level Dynu name and on the user's own domain; A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, SRV, TXT and PTR are free [1]
- binding note: the hostname cap of 4 decides for a free account; the record-type gate matters only for CAA-class records
- interface detail: three update paths: a dyndns2-style HTTP update, GET https://api.dynu.com/nic/update?hostname=HOST&myip=IP&myipv6=IPV6&password=PASSWORD (the password may be sent as is or as an MD5 or SHA256 hash, and a separate IP update password can be set), up to 20 hostnames per request; HTTP and TCP GnuDIP at gnudip.dynu.com; and a REST API at https://api.dynu.com/v2/ with an API-Key header that manages hostnames and DNS records
- tooling: the free Dynu IP update clients for Windows, macOS and Linux, ddclient with protocol dyndns2, routers with a Dynu or Custom provider, GnuDIP clients, and curl against the REST API
- composes with: a free name that can also carry MX, TXT, SRV and CNAME records and a wildcard, on a Dynu domain or on a domain the user already owns that is served by Dynu name servers
- reliability: a failed update authentication returns HTTP 200 with the body badauth, so a status-only check reports success on a failed update; an unknown domain name can also return badauth
- notes: Confirmation interval: none; the dynamic DNS page states that accounts never expire. The free hostname count is 4 in the FAQ and the membership page implies 3, so the figure needs a re-read.
- evidence note: the dynamic DNS page, the FAQ, the membership page, the REST API page and the IP update protocol page were read and quoted; the update endpoint was probed once with a wrong password and answered 200 badauth. The free hostname count is 4 in the FAQ and implied as 3 by the membership page, so the figure is unreconciled

## dynv6

- `domains-dns/dynv6` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding none | category free dynamic subdomain
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T02:05:09.544Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://dynv6.com/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/dynv6.md
- free tier: a free hostname for dynamic IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, or delegation of the user's own domain to dynv6, free for everyone; no zone or hostname count is published | unit: objects | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: unverified: no hostname, zone or record count is published on the pages read
- retention: unverified: no expiry, inactivity or confirmation rule is stated on the pages read | source: [1]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: the sign-up form has an email, a password of at least 8 characters and a password confirmation; no phone and no card field
- interface: rest
- binding note: no count, expiry or review is published, so no limit binds on the pages read; the stated exposure is that the service has no enterprise DDoS protection and no SLA
- interface detail: five ways to update a zone: a REST API, an update API, a DynDNS-compatible API, SSH with public key authentication, and DNS updates signed with TSIG keys; the DynDNS-style API updates the IPv4 address only; webhooks fire when the address changes
- tooling: curl, nsupdate or any software that speaks RFC 2136 with a TSIG key, a router's DynDNS client, or lego for certificate challenges
- composes with: a free name with a full update API; a zone under the vendor's suffix is not the registrant's, and the user's own domain can instead be delegated to dynv6
- reliability: the vendor says it offers no enterprise-grade DDoS protection and no SLA and asks that it not be used for critical services; the suffix is on the Public Suffix List, so the TLS limit counts per name
- notes: Nothing published binds: no count, expiry or review. The unknowns are the withdrawal rule and the count, and the vendor disclaims an SLA. The zone is the vendor's; delegating the user's own domain is the other offer. The TLS limit does not bind, because dynv6.net is listed.
- evidence note: the home page, the API page and the sign-up form were read and quoted; no count, expiry or suffix list was read; the TLS statement is an inference from the Let's Encrypt registered-domain rule and the Public Suffix List entry

## freemyip.com

- `domains-dns/freemyip` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence measured | binding retention-clamped | category free dynamic subdomain
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:10.325Z (live) | stale on 2027-02-02
- url https://freemyip.com/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/freemyip.md
- free tier: free dynamic DNS subdomains under freemyip.com, with no login, no ads and no expiration date stated on the home page; any subdomain of the name returns the same address | unit: objects | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: unverified: no count of subdomains per user or per address is published on the pages read
- retention: the subdomain can be kept as long as wanted if the address is updated at least once a year, even with the same address; a deleted subdomain cannot be created again for 12 months | days: 365 | source: [2]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: anonymous | detail: no login is required, according to the home page; the update URL carries a token and a domain, and the creation flow itself was not run
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - retention-clamped (binding): the address must be updated at least once a year, even when it has not changed, to keep the subdomain [2]
- binding note: the yearly update is the only stated limit; the count of names is unverified; no sign-up is asked, so the token returned at creation is the only handle, and the zone is the vendor's
- interface detail: one HTTPS GET to /update with token and domain parameters sets the address; optional parameters set an IPv4 or IPv6 address (myip), a TXT record (txt, also applied to every subdomain of the name), a verbose reply (verbose) or a delete (delete); the reply is the text OK or ERROR with HTTP status 200
- tooling: curl, a browser, a router or any scheduler that can request a URL
- composes with: a free name with a TXT parameter that the help page says also works for any subdomain of the name, so a DNS-01 challenge record can be set by inference; a CNAME or DNAME from the user's own domain can point at it; the zone is the vendor's, so it cannot be a Cloudflare zone
- reliability: an update with a token that does not exist returns HTTP 200 with the body 'ERROR' and a line naming the token, so a status-only check reports success on a failed update; the suffix is on the Public Suffix List, so the TLS limit counts per name
- notes: The only anonymous name in this set: no login, a token and a yearly update. The vendor's clock binds, not an owner's consent: a name lapses when the address is not updated for a year. The zone is the vendor's. The TLS limit does not bind, because the suffix is listed.
- evidence note: the update endpoint was called with a token that does not exist and answered 200 with an ERROR body, which proves the endpoint and the failure shape; the home and help pages were read and quoted; the creation flow was not run, because it makes a name

## Google Trust Services

- `domains-dns/google-trust-services` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding request-rate | category certificate authority | tier Public CA (Certificate Manager)
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:09.557Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-manager/docs/public-ca | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/google.md
- free tier: certificates from the Public CA ACME endpoint are free; the quota is 100 new orders per hour per Google Cloud project, with wildcard names over the DNS challenge | unit: requests | metered on: request-count | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no certificate size cap stated on the pages read; the quotas are on requests and not on objects | source: [1]
- retention: certificates are good for up to 90 days by default and a client may ask for as little as 1 day; the ACME account has no expiry, and an EAB secret must be used within 7 days | days: 90 | source: [2]
- egress: no charge | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: a Google Cloud project is required, and the Cloud Billing page says a project not linked to an active Cloud Billing account cannot use Google Cloud services even when they are free; that account is tied to a Google payments profile and a payment method; the Public CA tutorial lists no billing step, so whether the Public CA API can be enabled with no payment method on file is unverified: behind a sign-up (https://docs.cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/create-billing-account, https://docs.cloud.google.com/ruby/docs/reference/google-cloud-security-public_ca/latest)
- interface: rest, cli
- limits:
  - request-rate (binding): 100 new orders per hour per Google Cloud project, shared by all ACME accounts in that project [3]
  - request-rate (binding): 25 new accounts per minute and 100 per hour [3]
  - write-gated: an EAB secret is valid 7 days and registers one ACME account only [1]
  - retention-clamped: certificates are good for up to 90 days [2]
- binding note: 100 new orders per hour per project bounds issuance, far above one user's need; the billing link on the project is the gate that decides who can use it
- interface detail: ACME v2 at https://dv.acme-v02.api.pki.goog/directory (staging at https://dv.acme-v02.test-api.pki.goog/directory) with external account binding required; the EAB key is made with the Public CA API or gcloud publicca external-account-keys create
- tooling: certbot, acme.sh, any ACME client that supports EAB, the gcloud CLI for the EAB key
- composes with: a free ACME CA run by a different operator than Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL, with wildcard names over DNS-01 and certificates down to 1 day; the cost is a Google Cloud project that must be linked to a Cloud Billing account
- reliability: the ACME service does not support retrying a challenge, so a client requests a new authorization after a failed validation; no outage history was read
- notes: The 90-day figure is the default for the ACME endpoint. Certificate Manager's own Google-managed certificates are moving to 45 days, which is a different path from a client using ACME directly.
- evidence note: the Public CA tutorial, concepts page, quota page, Google blog and ACME divergence page were captured and quoted; the production directory answered 200 with externalAccountRequired true. The card requirement is read from the billing page and a client-library quick start and was not seen at a sign-up.

## Hetzner DNS

- `domains-dns/hetzner-dns` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding per-object-cap | category managed authoritative DNS | tier DNS in Hetzner Console
- needs card unknown, phone yes, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:07.606Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://www.hetzner.com/dns-console | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/hetzner.md
- free tier: DNS zones and records are managed in Hetzner Console and the API for free; up to 25 zones by default, up to 500 records per zone and 50 records per RRset; a domain you own is required | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: up to 500 records per zone and 50 records per RRset, the 500 raisable on a justified demand; up to 25 zones by default | source: [2]
- retention: a zone that is not delegated to the Hetzner name servers for more than 28 days is deleted automatically; nothing else is stated about inactivity | days: 28 | source: [3]
- egress: no DNS query cap published on the pages read | metered: no | source: [2]
- identity: email | detail: an account needs a valid e-mail address, personal or business contact information and a billing address, with a phone number optional; Hetzner may ask an account to verify before it processes an order, by a government ID copy or by a credit-card prepayment; unverified: whether creating a DNS zone triggers that verification (https://docs.hetzner.com/general/billing-and-account-management/account-getting-started/, https://docs.hetzner.com/general/security-and-identify/fraud-prevention-faq/)
- interface: rest, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap (binding): up to 500 records per zone, 50 records per RRset, 25 zones by default [2]
  - request-rate: 3600 API requests per hour per project, refilling 1 request per second [4]
  - retention-clamped: a zone not delegated to Hetzner name servers for more than 28 days is deleted [3]
- binding note: the owned-domain requirement and the 25-zone default decide; the record cap is not binding for a personal set of names
- interface detail: the Hetzner Cloud API at https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/ with an Authorization Bearer project token: POST /zones creates a zone, and POST /zones/{id_or_name}/rrsets/{rr_name}/{rr_type}/actions/set_records replaces the records of a record set; there is no dyndns2 or HTTP-GET update URL, so a dynamic update is an API call with a token; the default rate limit is 3600 requests per hour per project; zone names must be a registrable domain under a public suffix, not a subdomain
- tooling: curl, the hcloud CLI (hcloud zone create), BIND zone-file import, and AXFR secondary zones against an external primary
- composes with: a zone can also run as a secondary that copies a primary elsewhere by AXFR, and a zone can be shared across projects for managed certificates and load balancers; it cannot hold a name that is not a domain you own
- reliability: an undelegated zone is deleted after 28 days, and a new account can be asked for an ID copy or a card prepayment before it can order
- notes: Confirmation interval: none for a delegated zone; the only inactivity rule found is the 28-day deletion of a zone that is not delegated to Hetzner name servers. It is authoritative DNS for a domain the user already owns, not a free subdomain or a dynamic DNS hostname service.
- evidence note: the DNS Console page, the DNS overview and limits page, the creating-a-zone page, the DNS FAQ, the Cloud API reference and the account pages were read and quoted; the API was probed once without a token and answered 401. The 25-zone default is on the marketing page and the 500-record limit on the docs page

  - write-gated (binding): the service is in open beta and is limited to IPv6 certification or tunnelbroker account holders, colocation customers and transit customers; no record count and no query cap is published [1]
- interface detail: no record-management API is documented on dns.he.net or dns.he.net/docs.html; the programmatic path is the dyndns-compatible endpoint https://dyn.dns.he.net/nic/update?hostname=<record>&password=<key>&myip=<address> (GET, POST, or HTTP basic auth with the record name as the user), one request for IPv4 and one for IPv6, and txt= in place of myip= for a TXT record first created in the panel; the dynamic service is included free with a dns.he.net account; the update URL changes the address of an A or AAAA record, or the value of a TXT record, that already exists, and its interface term would be dyndns, which the vocabulary lacks, so interface carries unknown
- tooling: the web panel for zone and record management; the dyndns URL for dynamic A, AAAA and TXT records; no SDK and no documented REST API
- composes with: reverse DNS and secondary zones, which the other free providers in this set do not do as readily
- reliability: the registration form is withheld from some source networks, which receive 'Your IP address is not permitted to register at this time (This network is restricted)' in its place
- notes: An unpublished cap is a discretionary throttle. A design that depends on it has no ceiling to plan against, which is worse than a small published one. The interface field is 'unknown' rather than 'rest' because the only programmatic path is a key-based dyndns URL, which cannot create a zone or enumerate records.
- evidence note: the service page was read and states the eligibility gate and the dyndns syntax.

## is-a.dev

- `domains-dns/is-a-dev` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category free registrable subdomain
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:10.325Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://docs.is-a.dev/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/docs-2.md
- free tier: a free <name>.is-a.dev subdomain, registered by a pull request that adds one JSON file to the domains directory of the service's GitHub repository | unit: objects | metered on: none | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: no subdomain count per account is published on the pages read; only one single-letter subdomain per user is allowed
- retention: no expiry or renewal term is published; a subdomain lasts until the maintainers remove it or its JSON file is deleted by a pull request | source: [2]
- egress: no query cap published | metered: no | source: [3]
- identity: email | detail: a GitHub account of an individual; the only owner field the JSON file requires is the GitHub username, and a GitHub organisation account cannot register; no phone and no card are asked (https://docs.is-a.dev/domain-structure/)
- interface: git
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): every registration and every later change is a pull request that a maintainer reviews; the service states it can deny any request for any reason, and review time is volunteer time with no published figure [2]
  - write-gated (binding): NS records are approved only in specific cases and are refused to an account without an is-a.dev subdomain held for at least 30 days; review takes usually 24 to 72 hours and up to 2 weeks [3]
  - write-gated (binding): a root subdomain must belong to a software-development-related project; the eligibility is part of the review [2]
- binding note: the operator reviews each request and states it can terminate a subdomain at any time for any reason, so the owner can withdraw the name; the zone is the operator's and the registrant holds records only, apart from approved NS cases
- interface detail: every create, change or delete is a pull request against the register repository with a JSON file per name; the supported record types are A, AAAA, CAA, CNAME, DS, MX, SRV, TLSA, TXT and a service-specific URL redirector, and NS only in approved cases
- tooling: git and a GitHub account; a pull request for each change, merged by a maintainer
- composes with: a CNAME to a free static host gives a named site; the zone is not yours (NS delegation is refused to an account that has held a subdomain for under 30 days and is otherwise decided case by case), so it cannot become a Cloudflare zone of its own by default
- reliability: the operator can remove a subdomain at any time for any reason, the service is run by volunteers and the TLS limit is per name because the suffix is on the Public Suffix List
- notes: Withdrawal binds first: a maintainer's pull-request review stands between the request and the name, and the operator can end the name at any time. The zone is not the registrant's, so there is no own zone, no Cloudflare zone and no wildcard certificate for the subdomain by default. The TLS limit does not bind, because the suffix is listed and each name counts alone against the Let's Encrypt limit.
- evidence note: the domain-structure, FAQ, quickstart and terms pages were read and quoted; the TLS statement is an inference from the Let's Encrypt registered-domain rule and the suffix's listing in the captured Public Suffix List

## No-IP

- `domains-dns/no-ip-free` | qualifies-with-caveat | evidence documented | binding retention-clamped | category free dynamic DNS hostname | tier Free Dynamic DNS
- needs card no, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-03T16:43:07.606Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-04
- url https://www.noip.com/free | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/noip.md
- free tier: 1 hostname on a No-IP shared domain, no credit card; the hostname must be confirmed every 30 days or it is deleted | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 1 hostname on the free plan, on one of 30+ No-IP shared domains; the zone belongs to No-IP, so the user holds no record count of its own; hostnames may be type A, AAAA or Port 80 Redirect | source: [1]
- retention: a free hostname is active for 23 days, may be confirmed in the next 7 days, stops resolving when it expires, sits 14 more days in redemption and is then deleted and open to anyone; an update from a client does not confirm it | days: 30 | source: [2] | note: confirmation is a web login or an e-mailed link
- egress: no DNS query cap published on the pages read | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: the sign-up form asks for an e-mail address and a password and a terms checkbox that states one free account; the free page says no credit card is required (https://www.noip.com/sign-up, https://www.noip.com/free); no phone field in the captured form text
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - retention-clamped (binding): confirm every 30 days: active 23 days, 7-day confirmation window, 14-day redemption, then deletion [2]
  - per-object-cap: 1 hostname on the free plan [1]
- binding note: the 30-day manual confirmation is what decides; an update client keeps the address current but does not renew the hostname
- interface detail: a dyndns2-style HTTP update request, GET https://dynupdate.no-ip.com/nic/update?hostname=HOST&myip=IP with HTTP Basic auth (the account e-mail address and password), on port 443 over HTTPS or on ports 80 and 8245 over HTTP; the response is a text code such as good, nochg or badauth; the pages read list a RESTful API only under the contact-sales Branded Remote Access plan
- tooling: the free No-IP Dynamic Update Client for Windows, macOS and Linux, any dyndns2-compatible client or router, and curl from cron; confirmation itself is a web or e-mail action with no documented API
- composes with: a name for a changing address and nothing else on the free plan; the domains are No-IP's, so the name cannot be a zone of its own, and the 30-day confirmation has to be done by hand
- reliability: a free hostname silently stops resolving if the 30-day confirmation is missed; the update endpoint answers HTTP 401 with the body badauth for a request without credentials; a client without an approved User-Agent can be rate-limited or blocked, and the badagent and abuse codes tell a client to stop updating
- notes: Free confirmation interval: 30 days (23 active, 7 to confirm, then 14 in redemption). The paid Enhanced plan, USD 2.50 a month billed annually for 5 hostnames, lists hostnames that never expire.
- evidence note: the free-plan page, the confirmation knowledge-base page, the FAQ, the sign-up page and the update protocol pages were read and quoted; the unauthenticated update endpoint was probed once and answered 401 badauth
- evidence:
  - [1] 2026-11-03: the free plan lists 1 hostname | capture: sha256:b831197726766f7013fae7ea2a4e76a584182eef9bb06ad3822c877a22d55d15 | quote: 1 Hostname
  - [1] 2026-11-03: no credit card is required for the free plan | capture: sha256:b831197726766f7013fae7ea2a4e76a584182eef9bb06ad3822c877a22d55d15 | quote: When we say free, we actually mean free - no credit card required, ever.
  - [2] 2026-11-03: a free hostname must be confirmed every 30 days | capture: sha256:e5404f7962279e4a7449a46276e2cc110f9c88105734202368b48db80e7ed82a | quote: Free hostnames require confirmation every 30 days to remain active in your account.
  - [2] 2026-11-03: the confirmation window opens after 23 days and lasts 7 days | capture: sha256:e5404f7962279e4a7449a46276e2cc110f9c88105734202368b48db80e7ed82a | quote: After 23 days the hostname will enter a “Confirmation” period where it will be eligible to be confirmed for the next 7 days.

## Bunny DNS

- `domains-dns/bunny-dns` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding none | category managed authoritative DNS | tier DNS hosting, no query fees, USD 1 minimum monthly account usage
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-11-04T02:45:32.881Z (live) | stale on 2026-12-05
- url https://bunny.net/pricing/dns/ | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/bunny.md
- free tier: DNS hosting has no charge of its own for up to 500 zones per account and no per-query fee, but the account-wide USD 1 minimum monthly usage applies while a zone is active, so a DNS-only account pays USD 1 a month; a 14-day trial with trial credits and no payment card comes first | unit: objects | metered on: object-count | read on: 2026-11-03 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: 5,000 records per zone and 500 zones per account by default; both can be raised on request to sales | source: [2]
- retention: a trial account is disabled when the trial ends unless the balance is topped up; a negative balance disables the account and after 60 days the stored data is deleted | days: 60 | source: [3]
- egress: no per-query charges | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: trial sign-up needs an e-mail address confirmed by a link, and the trial credits come with no payment card; after the trial the account is disabled unless funds are added, by card, PayPal or crypto, from USD 10 (https://bunny.net/docs/quickstart.md, https://bunny.net/docs/billing/add-funds.md)
- interface: rest, cli
- limits:
  - per-object-cap: 5,000 records per zone and 500 zones per account [2]
- limits note: USD 1 minimum monthly usage across the whole account while a DNS zone is active; usage below USD 1 is rounded up to USD 1 for that month; recharge amounts start at USD 10
- binding note: no limit kind binds; a DNS-only account is charged the USD 1 monthly minimum, and a trial account is disabled when the trial ends unless funds are added
- interface detail: the bunny.net REST API v3 with an AccessKey header: PUT /dnszone/{zoneId}/records adds a record and POST /dnszone/{zoneId}/records/{id} updates one; no dyndns2 or other HTTP-GET update URL is documented in the pages read, so a dynamic update is a REST call with the record id
- tooling: curl against the REST API, the bunny CLI command bunny dns for zones and records, and BIND zone-file import
- composes with: scriptable DNS records answer queries with logic, and custom nameservers on the user's own domain are included at no extra cost
- reliability: an account whose trial has ended or whose balance is negative is disabled, and a disabled account does not keep its zones online; the stored data is deleted 60 days after a negative balance
- notes: Confirmation interval: none; there is no renewal or keep-alive step for a zone while the account is funded. The USD 1 minimum is shared with every other bunny.net product on the account. If DNS is the only service you use, you are still charged the $1 minimum for that month, and the minimum applies to the entire account, not per zone.
- evidence note: the DNS pricing page, the DNS and billing documentation, the limits page and the API reference were read and quoted; no sign-up form was submitted, so whether DNS zones can be created before the trial credits are used is as documented, not measured

- composes with: the anchor of the cheapest complete public endpoint: registrar plus free DNS plus free Universal SSL plus a free tunnel
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The .com row is the finding: USD 10.46 for registration and for renewal, with the ICANN fee inside the price. A promo registrar is cheaper in year one; from year two the renewal decides, so compare renewals with any ICANN fee charged on top added.
- evidence note: Cloudflare's own pages prove the at-cost model, that the ICANN fee is inside the price, the .uk transfer terms, and which TLDs are offered. The per-TLD prices come from a third-party table, cfdomainpricing.com, because Cloudflare's public search prices one name at a time as it is typed and publishes no per-TLD list. - per-object cap: not applicable: the unit is a domain name
- retention: a registration runs for its paid term and renews at the renewal-list price; a domain whose registrant email is not verified within 15 days is placed on clientHold | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable to a registrar | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: email | detail: sign-up asks an email address and a password behind a reCAPTCHA, or a Google or Facebook sign-in; each domain needs a contact profile with a name, an email address and a phone number, and the registrant email is verified by a link or a code within 15 days of the first notice, which is sent when a registration or transfer completes. No phone verification step is stated on the contact, email-verification, checkout, account-funding or API pages; the API lists the phone number as a required contact field with length and format rules. The checkout page lists the billing contact's name and address, an optional tax ID and the payment method. Payment by card, PayPal, Alipay, Venmo, Bitcoin or Account Funds, so no card is required. The crypto guide on NameSilo's blog documents the Bitcoin path as: log in, open the Account Funds Manager, add funds with Bitcoin or through the Nicky processor, wait for confirmation, then register from the balance at checkout; it lists no phone check or identity-document step and calls crypto purchases more private than card payments. The account-funding page lists Bitcoin without the 'verified' qualifier that the card, PayPal and Skrill sources carry, a card source is verified through the billing manager, and API orders are paid from a verified card or Account Funds. NameSilo's privacy page says proof of identification may be requested, its blog says new accounts making large purchases or registering from high-risk locations may meet payment holds or additional verification requirements, and its account-funding page says a balance can be withheld when the funding source is judged not legitimate; whether a Bitcoin or Account Funds order passes without a phone check or an identity-document review is unverified: behind a sign-up. A third-party report describes a card-payment fraud review that froze an account until a card photo and an identity document were supplied
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): the promotional price covers the first-year registration only; renewal is the regular price: .xyz USD 2.79 then USD 17.29, .vip USD 4.99 then USD 19.49, .cc USD 4.19 then USD 9.99, .eu USD 5.49 then USD 9.99, .org USD 10.79 then USD 14.99, .top USD 1.88 then USD 4.88 [3]
  - write-gated (binding): Discount Program prices (.com USD 12.00 instead of USD 19.99 at the 0+ tier) apply only to orders paid from Account Funds, topped up at USD 50.00 minimum [4]
- limits note: Transfer in: the transfer price list has no entry for .de, .eu or .uk, while the registration and renewal lists carry all three. For the extensions in the transfer list, one year is added to the expiry at no extra charge on completion; the FAQ names two exceptions, a renewal at the previous registrar within 45 days and a registry maximum (typically 10 years) that the extra year would exceed. A .uk transfer needs no authorization code: the order is followed by an IPS tag change to NAMESILO at the previous registrar. What a cart charges for a .de, .eu or .uk transfer, and whether it adds a year, is unverified: behind a sign-up.
- binding note: the renewal price decides what a name costs to keep; the first-year promotion and the Account Funds requirement are payment gates, not quotas
- interface detail: a web dashboard and an HTTP API whose getPrices operation returns the price list; API access carries no extra charge, and the site menu links an MCP server at mcp.namesilo.com
- tooling: the NameSilo API, the dashboard, the MCP server at mcp.namesilo.com
- composes with: a registrar only: WHOIS privacy, email forwarding and DNS management are included at no charge, and the nameservers can point at any free DNS host; .de at USD 5.99 costs the same in the first year and every renewal; .uk is USD 2.25 in the first year and USD 6.49 at renewal
- reliability: a 2023 third-party report: an account was frozen after a failed virtual-card top-up and unblocked once a card photo and a passport were supplied; support said most virtual cards are not supported
- notes: Retail USD, first year / renewal / transfer-in: .com 19.99 / 19.99 / 11.50 (transfer normal price 11.50); .org 10.79 (regular 14.99) / 14.99 / 11.99; .net 15.95 / 15.95 / 11.35 (transfer normal price 15.95); .xyz 2.79 (regular 17.29) / 17.29 / 14.75; .top 1.88 (regular 4.88) / 4.88 / 4.78; .de 5.99 / 5.99 / not listed; .eu 5.49 (regular 9.99) / 9.99 / not listed; .uk 2.25 (regular 6.49) / 6.49 / not listed, moved in by changing the IPS tag to NAMESILO; .cc 4.19 (regular 9.99) / 9.99 / 9.49; .vip 4.99 (regular 19.49) / 19.49 / 16.50. Discount Program 0+ tier, first year / renewal: .com 12.00 / 12.00; .org 9.29 / 13.49; .net 11.85 / 11.85; .xyz 2.69 / 17.19; .top 1.78 / 4.78; .de 5.89 / 5.89; .eu 5.39 / 9.89; .uk 2.15 (regular 6.39) / 6.39; .cc 4.09 / 9.89; .vip 4.89 / 19.39. The .com transfer-in at 11.50 is below both .com renewal prices. Renewal is never above the regular registration rate except .mobi and promotions.
- evidence note: Prices and terms are read from NameSilo's own price lists, product lists, pricing page, transfer page, crypto guide and support pages. The transfer price list has no entry for .de, .eu or .uk, so their transfer price, and whether a transfer adds a year, are unverified: behind a sign-up (a cart read). Whether a Bitcoin or Account Funds order passes without a phone check or an identity-document review is unverified: behind a sign-up; the documented crypto path lists no phone check or identity-document step, and the card fraud-review gate is a third-party report. A signed-in cart read of a .de, .eu and .uk transfer, and a signed-in checkout paid with Bitcoin and with Account Funds, would move these up. The .com and .uk price fields were re-read from the current price lists.

## Porkbun

- `domains-dns/porkbun` | paid-only | evidence documented | binding write-gated | category domain registrar
- needs card yes, phone no, ID no, institution no | verified 2026-10-30T11:09:01.006Z (live) | stale on 2026-11-30
- url https://porkbun.com/products/domains | page https://fshy.ajam.dev/p/porkbun.md
- price USD 11.08 .com; USD 7.98 .org; USD 2.04 then USD 14.21 .xyz
- free tier: not free. Promotional first-year prices with a separate renewal price | unit: none | metered on: none | read on: 2026-10-22 | source: [1]
- per-object cap: not applicable: the unit is a domain name
- retention: a registration runs for its term and renews at the regular price shown on the TLD page | source: [2]
- egress: not applicable to a registrar | metered: no | source: [1]
- identity: card | detail: a payment method
- interface: rest
- limits:
  - write-gated (binding): the promo price applies to the first year only; the renewal is the regular price [2]
- interface detail: a web dashboard, an API for registered domains, and a public pricing endpoint (api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3/pricing/get) that answers without an API key
- tooling: the Porkbun API, the dashboard
- composes with: a cheaper first year than Cloudflare on .org, and a more expensive second year on .xyz
- reliability: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
- notes: The .xyz promo is 2.04 and the renewal is 14.21, which is seven times the first year and more than a .com at Cloudflare. The promo is the marketing; the renewal is the price.
- evidence note: the price index, the TLD pages and the public pricing API give registration, renewal and transfer separately, in USD with the ICANN fee included, and mark each sale price
- extras:
  - tld_price_terms: USD; non-premium names, one-year registration, renewal and transfer; most transfers include a one-year renewal
  - icann_fee: included in every listed price, with any other fee
  - tld_coupons: none: the pricing API returns an empty coupons list for each of .com, .org, .net, .xyz, .top, .de, .eu, .uk, .cc and .vip
  - tld_prices.com: first year USD 11.08; renewal USD 11.08; transfer USD 11.08; no sale price
  - tld_prices.org: first year USD 7.98 (first-year sale; USD 11.84 without it); renewal USD 11.84; transfer USD 11.84
  - tld_prices.net: first year USD 12.52; renewal USD 12.52; transfer USD 12.52; no sale price
  - tld_prices.xyz: first year USD 2.04 (first-year sale; USD 14.21 without it); renewal USD 14.21; transfer USD 14.21
  - tld_prices.top: first year USD 1.63 (first-year sale; USD 4.32 without it); renewal USD 4.63; transfer USD 4.63
  - tld_prices.de: first year USD 2.90 (sale; USD 5.49 regular registration); renewal USD 4.07; transfer USD 5.10
  - tld_prices.eu: first year USD 5.88; renewal USD 5.88; transfer USD 5.88; no sale price
  - tld_prices.uk: first year USD 5.66; renewal USD 5.66; transfer USD 0.00; no sale price
  - tld_prices.cc: first year USD 3.40 (sale; USD 8.55 without it); renewal USD 8.55; transfer USD 8.55
  - tld_prices.vip: first year USD 4.12 (first-year sale; USD 15.96 without it); renewal USD 5.15 and transfer USD 5.15, both sale prices over a struck USD 15.96
